_doc: Machine-readable copy of PDF Section A. NEVER edit requirement wording (only the owner may). Only passes and links may change. Owner chat additions are origin=owner_chat and are kept apart from PDF text. Generated by tools/bt/seed_register.py.

R01.text: A Total War-style, Hollywood-grade CGI animation of the entire Battle of Gettysburg from start to finish that anyone can fly around freely and watch any spot at any moment.

R02.text: A 1:1 3D digital recreation of the 1863 battlefield (terrain, rocks, hills, fences, earthworks, gun emplacements, trees, buildings, roads).

R03.text: 100% historically accurate hyper-realistic visuals, sounds, combat mechanics, environment.

R04.text: Individual units in hyper-realistic combat; every unit’s uniform and equipment correct; commanders lieutenant to general with correct appearance.

R05.text: Animation of preparatory events such as Buford scouting, soldiers building earthworks, casualties, casualties carried to field hospitals.

R06.text: Empty woods where nothing is happening, but accurate gunfire and artillery sound audible from anywhere with correct distance.

R07.text: The entire battle from start to finish.

R08.text: Remove all owner-supplied-input dependencies. Claude Code does everything itself, using the owner’s GPU as hard as needed. Physical capture is replaced by autonomous equivalents, clearly labeled; the only owner acts are the one-time account, credential, billing and licence steps in Part D.8.

R09.text: Be incredibly efficient with the owner’s usage while making rapid but totally accurate progress.

R10.text: Research what each individual unit wore, the different types of soldiers in each unit including sharpshooters, and how their uniforms, equipment and weapons looked; if a unit carried a specific rifle (the Springfield variants, Sharps rifles, and so on), say so.

R11.text: A greatly expanded master timeline, the backbone for scripting.

R12.text: Identify any and all reputable terrain sources for a July 1863 landscape, modern and from the 1860s.

R13.text: Far more detail about every 1863 terrain element: buildings, fences, earthworks, defenses, gun positions, field hospitals and the rest.

R14.text: If a fence existed at the start and was damaged during the battle, the animation shows that damage at the right time. Earthworks are not pre-placed; they are shown being constructed.

R17.text: Every soldier has a historically accurate, realistic appearance for how that soldier would have been dressed and equipped (not a photo replica of a real person). Every unit shows what it was actually doing at each time, including marching to fighting positions. Units that arrived on day 2 must not appear before they arrived.

R18.text: A 24/7 day and night animation. Night is clearly night with a dimmed sky, but everything and all activity stays visible, only dimmer. Soldiers are shown doing whatever they were doing at night: sitting around a fire, digging defenses, and so on.

R19.text: Users can navigate back and forth to different points in the battle.

R20.text: Research how trees and plant growth looked during the battle, as accurately as all known knowledge allows.

R21.text: Read the full free online library of primary sources, witness accounts, biographies and more; audit everything for accuracy; take the animation’s historical accuracy as far as that library allows.

R22.text: The default film path ends with the July 4 events at Gettysburg (casualty collection, burial, the truce, the Confederate withdrawal). At the end of July 4 the animation swirls and jumps to the Gettysburg cemetery on November 19, 1863, and from the point of view of a person in the front row shows an accurate version of Lincoln taking the stage and giving the Gettysburg Address. Events outside Gettysburg are not shown. Specified in B.12.
